CTE MATERIALIZED keyword.mapping:
ALWAYS use AS MATERIALIZED for CTEs that scope instances by campus, location, or any multi-table filter chain. Without MATERIALIZED, PostgreSQL 12+ may inline the CTE and make catastrophic join order decisions on large tables.

Example:
WITH sc_instances AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT inst.id, inst.hrid, inst.title
    FROM inventory.instance__t inst
    WHERE EXISTS (...)
)

This forces PostgreSQL to:
1. Execute the CTE first and store results in memory/temp
2. Use accurate row counts for subsequent query planning
3. Prevent the optimizer from flattening CTEs into joins that trigger full seq scans on 10M+ row tables

LDP column type mismatch.mapping:
CRITICAL: In LDP/MetaDB, large fact tables store foreign key columns as TEXT while small reference/lookup tables store primary keys as UUID. This causes "operator does not exist: text = uuid" or "operator does not exist: uuid = text" errors if you join without casting.

AFFECTED COLUMNS:
  holdings_record__t.instance_id → TEXT (target instance__t.id is UUID)
  item__t.holdings_record_id → TEXT (target holdings_record__t.id is UUID)
  item__t.effective_location_id → TEXT (target location__t.id is UUID)
  item__t.permanent_location_id → TEXT (target location__t.id is UUID)
  item__t.material_type_id → TEXT (target material_type__t.id is UUID)
  audit_loan__t.loan__item_id → UUID (target item__t.id type varies; cast BOTH sides)

FIX — cast the UUID side to TEXT:
  hr.instance_id = inst.id::text, ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id::text,
  ii.effective_location_id = loc.id::text, ii.material_type_id = imt.id::text

NO CAST for UUID=UUID lookup joins:
  loc.library_id = lib.id, lib.campus_id = camp.id

MARC data.mapping:
When a user asks about MARC fields or MARC records, use marctab.mtNNN per-field tables (e.g. marctab.mt245 for title, marctab.mt300 for physical description). Each table has columns: srs_id, instance_hrid, instance_id, field, ind1, ind2, ord, sf (subfield code), content (subfield value).

To extract a specific subfield, use SCALAR SUBQUERIES — NOT LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY:
  GOOD (index probe per instance, EXPLAIN cost ~16K across 257K instances):
    (SELECT m.content FROM marctab.mt300 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = si.hrid AND m.sf = 'a' LIMIT 1) AS extent_300a
  BAD (full table scan + merge join on millions of rows, cost ~2.1M):
    LEFT JOIN marctab.mt245 m245 ON m245.instance_hrid = sbi.hrid ... GROUP BY ... MAX(CASE WHEN m245.sf = 'a' ...)

Prefer marctab.mtNNN over the folio_source_record.marctab VIEW for reliable performance.

When a user says "show me the MARC record" or "expand the MARC data", either:
  (a) Use scalar subqueries from the specific marctab.mtNNN tables for the fields they care about, OR
  (b) Use folio_source_record.records__t.parsed_record__content for the complete raw MARC JSON.

MARC field.mapping:
A specific MARC tag number (e.g. 245, 300, 650). Use the corresponding marctab.mtNNN table:
  marctab.mt245 for field 245, marctab.mt300 for field 300, marctab.mt650 for field 650, etc.

Subfields are ROWS — each row has sf (subfield code) and content (subfield value). There are NO sf_a, sf_b, sf_c columns.
  Example: (SELECT m.content FROM marctab.mt245 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid AND m.sf = 'a' LIMIT 1)

ord column distinguishes repeated fields (e.g. first 650 has ord=1, second has ord=2).

To check if a MARC field EXISTS:
  WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marctab.mt300 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid)

To check if a MARC field DOES NOT EXIST:
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marctab.mt300 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid)

Prefer marctab.mtNNN over folio_source_record.marctab WHERE field = 'NNN' for reliable performance and Index Only Scan eligibility.

MARC query with item filter performance.mapping:
When a MARC query also filters by item-level attributes (material type, item status, location), the TWO biggest performance factors are:

1. idx_item_holdings_material index on inventory.item__t(holdings_record_id, material_type_id) â€” turns each nested EXISTS probe from a 10M-row seq scan into an index seek. Without this index, the item__t EXISTS check alone can take minutes.

2. AS MATERIALIZED on the instance-scoping CTE â€” prevents PostgreSQL from inlining the CTE and making bad join-order decisions against the marctab view.

Both are required for sub-second performance on queries like "Smith College books missing MARC field 300". If the query times out, check that the composite index exists:
  SELECT indexname FROM pg_indexes WHERE tablename = 'item__t' AND indexdef LIKE '%holdings_record_id%material_type_id%';

If missing, create it:
  CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_item_holdings_material ON inventory.item__t (holdings_record_id, material_type_id);

MARC record.mapping: MARC bibliographic data is stored in folio_source_record.records__t.parsed_record__content as a TEXT column (NOT JSONB). It contains a JSON string representation of the MARC record. To check if a MARC field exists (e.g. field 300), use: parsed_record__content ILIKE '%"300"%'. To check if a field does NOT exist: parsed_record__content NOT ILIKE '%"300"%'. To search for a specific subfield value: parsed_record__content ILIKE '%"650"%somevalue%'. NEVER use jsonb_exists(), jsonb_path_query(), ->> operator, or any JSONB functions on this column â€” it is TEXT. NEVER cast it to JSONB â€” the content is too large and the cast will timeout. Always use ILIKE/NOT ILIKE pattern matching for MARC field queries. Join to instances via: folio_source_record.records__t.external_ids_holder__instance_id = inventory.instance__t.id.

ORDER BY policy.mapping: Do NOT add ORDER BY to generated SQL unless the user explicitly requests sorted or ranked results (e.g. "top 10", "highest", "sorted by", "alphabetical"). ORDER BY forces PostgreSQL to materialize and sort the ENTIRE result set before returning a single row. On large datasets this adds massive overhead even with LIMIT 100. ORDER BY is appropriate for: ranking queries (ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 20), top-N queries, explicit sort requests. ORDER BY is NOT appropriate for: existence checks, missing-field reports, general list queries.

academic year.mapping: When a user says 'current year', 'this year', or 'academic year', they mean the academic/fiscal year running July 1 through June 30. To calculate the current academic year dynamically, ALWAYS use a CTE with the WITH keyword: WITH academic_year_dates AS ( SELECT CASE WHEN CURRENT_DATE >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months' THEN date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months' ELSE date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) - INTERVAL '6 months' END AS start_date, CASE WHEN CURRENT_DATE >= date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months' THEN date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '1 year' + INTERVAL '6 months' - INTERVAL '1 day' ELSE date_trunc('year', CURRENT_DATE) + INTERVAL '6 months' - INTERVAL '1 day' END AS end_date ) â€” then reference it with: JOIN academic_year_dates ayd ON TRUE and filter with: WHERE date_column >= ayd.start_date AND date_column <= ayd.end_date. call number ranges.mapping:
When grouping or counting by call number range or classification, NEVER use LEFT(call_number, 1) as a range â€” this incorrectly groups all LC classes starting with H (H, HA, HB, HC, HF, HQ, etc.) into one bucket and completely mishandles Dewey numbers.

Use this CASE expression to extract call number class correctly:

CASE
    -- LC Call Number: extract the leading letter(s) only (1-3 letters before the first digit)
    WHEN effective_call_number_components__call_number ~ '^[A-Z]{1,3}[0-9]'
    THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(effective_call_number_components__call_number, '^([A-Z]{1,3})[0-9].*', '\1')
    -- Dewey Call Number: extract the 3-digit hundred class (e.g. 823.914 â†’ 800)
    WHEN effective_call_number_components__call_number ~ '^[0-9]'
    THEN LPAD(
            CAST(
                FLOOR(CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(effective_call_number_components__call_number, '^([0-9]+).*', '\1') AS NUMERIC) / 100) * 100
            AS TEXT),
         3, '0')
    ELSE 'Unknown'
END AS call_number_class

LC examples:
  'H 123'    â†’ 'H'
  'HA 456'   â†’ 'HA'
  'HF 1234'  â†’ 'HF'
  'QA 76'    â†’ 'QA'
  'PS 3561'  â†’ 'PS'

Dewey examples:
  '823.914'  â†’ '800'
  '153.4'    â†’ '100'
  '372.6'    â†’ '300'

When asked for "call number range" or "call number prefix" or "classification", apply this CASE expression. When asked for a broader grouping (LC subclass description like "H = Social Sciences"), also provide a label by JOINing or CASE-matching the extracted class against known LC class descriptions.

When a user asks which call number RANGES have the highest circulation, use this expression in the GROUP BY and SELECT. Do NOT use LEFT(..., 1) or SUBSTRING(..., 1, 1).

When querying items by holdings or material type, ALWAYS structure queries to take advantage of this index:
- Drive from holdings â†’ items using holdings_record_id (index leading column)
- Filter by material_type_id in the same lookup (index second column)
- Use nested EXISTS (not JOIN + DISTINCT) so PostgreSQL can do index-only semi-join probes
- NEVER scan item__t first and then join back to holdings â€” that forces a 10M+ row seq scan

CAVEAT: LDP/MetaDB rebuilds tables nightly. If the index is dropped during refresh, re-create it via a post-refresh script or cron job.

The ONLY default indexes on item__t are:
- item__t_id_idx (id)
- item__t___id_idx (__id)

Without idx_item_holdings_material, any EXISTS or JOIN through holdings_record_id does a full sequential scan.

marctab.mapping:
MARC data is accessed via the marctab schema, which has one table per MARC field: marctab.mt000 through marctab.mt999.

Each table has columns: srs_id, instance_hrid, instance_id, field, ind1, ind2, ord, sf (subfield code like 'a', 'b'), content (subfield value). There are NO sf_a, sf_b, etc. columns.

Subfields are ROWS (not columns): filter by m.sf = 'a' and read m.content.

Join to inventory via: marctab.mtNNN.instance_hrid = inventory.instance__t.hrid

NOTE: There is a VIEW called folio_source_record.marctab that unions all ~1000 tables. PostgreSQL can sometimes prune this to a single underlying table, but mtNNN is preferred for guaranteed performance and Index Only Scan eligibility.

Examples:
  - Check field 300 exists: EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM marctab.mt300 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid)
  - Get ISBN: (SELECT m.content FROM marctab.mt020 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid AND m.sf = 'a' LIMIT 1)
  - Get title: (SELECT m.content FROM marctab.mt245 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid AND m.sf = 'a' LIMIT 1)

marctab per-field table structure.mapping:
The marctab schema contains one table per MARC field: marctab.mt000 through marctab.mt999. Each table contains ONLY rows for that MARC tag.

Columns per table: srs_id (UUID), instance_hrid (text, links to inventory.instance__t.hrid), instance_id (UUID), field (tag, e.g. '300'), ind1, ind2, ord (occurrence number for repeated fields), sf (subfield code, e.g. 'a', 'b'), content (subfield value text).

Subfields are ROWS (not columns). Each row is one subfield occurrence.
To get 245$a title: SELECT m.content FROM marctab.mt245 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = inst.hrid AND m.sf = 'a' LIMIT 1
For multiple subfields, use scalar subqueries per subfield (see hint 'marctab performance rule').

NEVER use folio_source_record.marctab (the VIEW) — always use marctab.mtNNN directly for guaranteed performance.

marctab performance rule.mapping:
CRITICAL PERFORMANCE RULE for MARC queries (EXPLAIN-verified 2026-03-13):

1. ALWAYS use marctab.mtNNN per-field tables (e.g. marctab.mt300, marctab.mt245).
   Columns: srs_id, instance_hrid, instance_id, field, ind1, ind2, ord, sf, content.
   Indexed on instance_hrid. NOT EXISTS check: Index Only Scan at cost ~0.74/probe.

2. For subfield extraction, use SCALAR SUBQUERIES — NOT LEFT JOIN + GROUP BY:
   GOOD (cost ~16K overhead for 257K instance set):
     (SELECT m.content FROM marctab.mt245 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = si.hrid AND m.sf = 'a' LIMIT 1) AS title_a
     (SELECT m.content FROM marctab.mt300 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = si.hrid AND m.sf = 'a' LIMIT 1) AS extent_a
   BAD (cost ~2.1M — full table scans + merge joins on 25M+ rows):
     LEFT JOIN marctab.mt245 m245 ON m245.instance_hrid = sbi.hrid ... GROUP BY ... MAX(CASE WHEN m245.sf = 'a' ...)

3. For repeated fields (e.g. all 650 subjects), use a scalar subquery with STRING_AGG:
     (SELECT STRING_AGG(m.content, ' ; ' ORDER BY m.ord) FROM marctab.mt650 m WHERE m.instance_hrid = si.hrid AND m.sf = 'a')

4. For complete raw MARC output, use folio_source_record.records__t.parsed_record__content.

5. Combine with MATERIALIZED CTEs and nested EXISTS for instance scoping (see hints 190, 192).

6. The folio_source_record.marctab VIEW can sometimes optimize via branch pruning but mtNNN is preferred for guaranteed performance.

marctab_join_safety.mapping: CRITICAL: marctab.mtNNN tables have instance_id as UUID type but inventory.instance__t.id may be TEXT type. Joining on these columns causes ERROR: operator does not exist: uuid = text. ALWAYS join on instance_hrid instead: marctab.mtNNN.instance_hrid = inventory.instance__t.hrid (both text, safe to compare). This applies to ALL marctab tables (mt000â€“mt999).

material type.mapping: inventory.material_type__t.name - user-facing resource category or document type (Book, Journal, Thesis/Dissertation, DVD/Blu-ray, etc.). Use this for book/journal/thesis filters, not instance_type__t.

nested EXISTS pattern for instance-level.mapping:
CRITICAL PERFORMANCE RULE: When building instance-level result sets with item-level filters (material type, item status, etc.), ALWAYS use nested EXISTS with MATERIALIZED CTEs. Never use JOIN + DISTINCT.

PATTERN:
WITH result AS MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT inst.id, inst.hrid, inst.title
    FROM inventory.instance__t inst
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM inventory.holdings_record__t hr
        WHERE hr.instance_id = inst.id::text
          AND [any holdings-level filters]
          AND EXISTS (
              SELECT 1
              FROM inventory.item__t ii
              WHERE ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id::text
                AND [any item-level filters like material_type_id]
          )
    )
)

This pattern:
1. Uses the index on holdings_record__t(instance_id) to find holdings for each instance
2. Uses the composite index idx_item_holdings_material on item__t(holdings_record_id, material_type_id) to check items
3. EXISTS is a semi-join â€” stops at first match per instance
4. MATERIALIZED prevents the planner from inlining the CTE and making bad join order decisions

For material type filtering, resolve the material_type_id with a scalar subquery:
  ii.material_type_id = (SELECT id FROM inventory.material_type__t WHERE LOWER(name) = 'book' LIMIT 1)

This avoids joining the material_type__t table into the main query, which can confuse the planner.

no_uuid_cast.mapping:
CRITICAL — NEVER CAST TO ::uuid. In LDP/MetaDB, large fact tables store FK columns as TEXT while reference table PKs are UUID. Casting to ::uuid causes: "operator does not exist: uuid = text".

ALWAYS cast the UUID PK side to TEXT:
  hr.instance_id = inst.id::text, ii.holdings_record_id = hr.id::text,
  ii.effective_location_id = loc.id::text, ii.permanent_location_id = loc.id::text,
  al.loan__item_id::text = ii.id::text, sr.external_id = inst.id::text,
  ii.material_type_id = imt.id::text

NO CAST NEEDED for lookup-to-lookup joins (UUID=UUID natively):
  loc.library_id = lib.id, lib.campus_id = camp.id

::uuid is NEVER the correct cast anywhere in this system.

query performance optimization.mapping: CRITICAL PERFORMANCE AND CORRECTNESS RULES: (1) Use circulation.audit_loan__t for counting checkouts â€” it has one row per loan EVENT. Filter with loan__action IN ('checkedout', 'checkedOutThroughOverride'). Columns use the loan__ prefix: loan__item_id, loan__action, loan__loan_date. (2) Do NOT use circulation.loan__t for counting checkouts â€” it stores the CURRENT STATE of each loan. A returned book has action='checkedin', so filtering action='checkedout' misses all returned items. Only use loan__t for "what is currently checked out right now" queries. (3) When a query uses CTEs (WITH clauses) that aggregate large tables, ALWAYS define a target_items CTE FIRST that applies all WHERE filters (location, campus, material type, etc.), then JOIN the circulation/notes CTEs to target_items. BAD pattern (timeout): CTE aggregates ALL rows, outer query filters. GOOD pattern (fast): target_items CTE with filters first, then circulation CTE joins to target_items. (4) NEVER use renewal_count IS NULL to filter initial checkouts â€” in FOLIO, initial checkouts have renewal_count = 0, not NULL. The loan__action filter alone is sufficient to identify checkouts.
